comments.body:
Fix pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1479 (change 1479).

Added a `make venv` target that provisions .venv with `uv venv --python <pinned>` and FAILS
loudly (naming the version and the `uv python install` remedy) rather than falling back to
ambient python3. `make worktree` now delegates to it before the already-correct `make install`.

The version is single-sourced in `.github/python-version.txt` (3.12), the same discipline as
`.github/git-version-floor.txt`. `tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py` holds it to the CI
matrix in _build-and-test.yml AND to the actions/setup-python pins, so dropping 3.12 from CI
reddens a test instead of silently leaving fresh venvs on an untested rev.

Verified end-to-end: `make venv` in a scratch tree produced Python 3.12.13 while this host's
ambient python3 is 3.14.6.

Re-check of the two failures this bug was found through, on Python 3.12.13 (the last AC):
  - tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present
    -> PASSES. It was an artifact of the untested interpreter. No ticket needed.
  - tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone
    -> STILL FAILS (assert 0 >= 1) with jscpd 5.0.14 installed. Genuinely unrelated to the
       Python rev, so filed as a real bug: 4bf4 (exultant-pinelike-prairiedog), linked
       discovered_from this ticket.

Docs updated: docs/local-dev-env.md gained a 'provision the venv on the Python CI tests'
prerequisite section mirroring the Git-floor one, and AGENTS.md's Codex bootstrap line now says
`make venv` instead of `python3 -m venv .venv`.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`Makefile` line 128 (the `worktree` target) provisions the new worktree's venv with:

    python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && $(MAKE) install

It inherits whatever `python3` resolves to on the host. Nothing pins or checks the version, and
`requires-python = ">=3.11"` (pyproject.toml:16) accepts anything from 3.11 upward, so
`uv sync --locked` succeeds and the mismatch is silent.

## Measured on this host 2026-08-05

    system python3            -> Python 3.14.6   (/opt/homebrew/bin/python3)
    CI matrix                 -> 3.11, 3.12, 3.13   (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml)
    worktree c6c9-attest-split/.venv      -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree rebar-8a5e/.venv             -> Python 3.14.6
    worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile/.venv    -> Python 3.14.6
    main checkout .venv                   -> Python 3.12.13

Every worktree created by `make worktree` runs **3.14.6, which CI never tests**. The main
checkout is on a tested version only by accident of WHEN it was created — its venv predates the
host's python3 moving to 3.14.

## The cost, which is not hypothetical

This is the canonical local-vs-CI divergence, and it burned real time tonight. Multiple agents
working in fresh worktrees hit local test failures that CI did not reproduce, then each spent
cycles proving them "pre-existing and environment-specific" -- correctly, but only after the
fact. Two failures repeatedly implicated:

    tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present
    tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone

Each agent rediscovered this independently. The failure mode is corrosive rather than loud:
local red that CI does not show trains agents (and humans) to discount local failures
generally, which is exactly backwards -- the next genuine local-only regression gets waved
through with the same reasoning.

It also cuts the other way: a change that breaks on 3.11 but passes on the developer's 3.14
looks clean locally and only fails after push, which is the slowest possible place to learn it.

## Note on scope

The version floor is separately declared and enforced for **git** (ticket 980d added
`.github/git-version-floor.txt` plus a conftest session-abort). There is no equivalent for
Python, even though Python is the far more likely source of behavioral divergence.

## Candidate approaches (weigh; not prescribed)

1. Pin the worktree venv to a CI-tested interpreter, e.g. `uv venv --python 3.12` (uv can fetch
   it), so a fresh worktree matches the matrix by construction.
2. Warn or fail loudly in `make worktree` / `make install` when the resolved interpreter is
   outside the CI matrix, naming the mismatch. Cheapest, and mirrors the git-floor pattern
   980d already established.
3. Add the host's version to the CI matrix -- rejected as stated, since it grows CI cost for
   every contributor to accommodate one machine, and does not stop the next drift.

Option 2 alone leaves the developer to act; option 1 removes the failure mode. They compose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A venv created by `make worktree` runs a Python version the CI matrix actually tests, or
      the command fails/warns explicitly naming the mismatch and the supported set.
- [x] The supported set is single-sourced from the CI matrix rather than duplicated, so adding
      or dropping a version in CI cannot silently desynchronize the check (the same
      single-sourcing discipline as `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and
      `.github/git-version-floor.txt`).
- [x] A test proves the check fires for an out-of-matrix interpreter and stays silent for an
      in-matrix one.
- [x] `docs/local-dev-env.md` states the supported Python versions and how to provision a
      matching venv when the host default differs.
- [x] The two failures listed above are re-checked on an in-matrix interpreter and either
      confirmed genuinely pre-existing or filed as real bugs -- right now nobody knows which,
      because every observation of them has been on an untested Python.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the a573 agent, which noticed its worktree venv was 3.14.6 while explaining three
local-only test failures. Independently verified here: system python3, the Makefile line, three
worktree venvs, and the CI matrix all measured directly.

file_impact.reason: new single-source pin for the dev interpreter version (3.12), mirroring git-version-floor.txt
new pinned venv target; worktree delegates to it instead of python3 -m venv
RED-first contracts: make venv asks for the pin, fails loudly without fallback, pin stays inside the CI matrix and setup-python pins
document the supported Python versions and how to provision a matching venv
Codex bootstrap line now says make venv, not python3 -m venv

compiled_state.title: make worktree builds its venv from ambient python3, so fresh worktrees run a Python CI never tests
